ask_withdrawn.meaning: the assistant tells the user there is nothing for them to do or decide now, or that it will not ask them anything further (takes back an earlier question)

remind_ask.meaning: the user asks to be reminded, notified, woken or told at some time

schedule_ask.meaning: the user asks the assistant to schedule something — to set it up to run later or on its own at a time it picks (schedule it, book it in, set it to run)

time_every.meaning: a repeating schedule: every day, every morning, hourly, weekly, every Monday, every month, every year

time_when.meaning: a day or a time of day for something to happen: tomorrow, tonight, next week, this Friday, the names of the weekdays, the morning of, the day before, o'clock

time_unit.meaning: a unit of time written right after a number (every form the language uses after a number): minutes, hours, days, weeks, o'clock

remind_stop.meaning: the user asks to stop, cancel, pause or turn off their reminders or alerts — give each in the word orders people use (verb first and noun first, e.g. «stop the reminders» and «reminders off»)

remind_decline.meaning: the user says they don't need or want a reminder or alert — no reminder needed, don't set a reminder, skip the alert (a statement, not a question)

stop_bare.meaning: a whole message that only says stop / that's enough

price_below.meaning: a price or value going below a line: below, under, less than, drops to, falls under, gets cheaper

price_above.meaning: a price or value going above a line: above, over, more than, exceeds, rises above

memory_forget.meaning: the user asks the assistant to forget or delete something it remembers about them

health.meaning: health and medical words (private — never stored in memory): hospital, illness, diagnosis, prescription, surgery, depression, diabetes, blood pressure, therapy

faith_politics.meaning: religion and politics words (private — never stored in memory): church, temple, mosque, religion, election, political party, vote

password_word.meaning: the words for password, PIN and one-time code as people write them just before the secret itself

bank_word.meaning: the words for bank, bank account and account number as people write them just before the number

my_name_is.meaning: words a person writes right before their own name to introduce themselves

confused.meaning: the user did not understand the answer or asks for simpler words

not_right.meaning: the user says the last answer was wrong, missed the point or still doesn't work, or asks to try again

glossary_ask.meaning: the user tells the assistant which word to use instead of another word

connect_verb.meaning: to connect or link an account, an AI or a key

disconnect_verb.meaning: to disconnect, unlink or remove a connected account or key

heavy_task.meaning: a request that needs careful work: code, analysis, a plan or strategy, a comparison, a design, a report or document, a spreadsheet, a summary, a translation, a why-question, a review, a contract, an essay

risk_task.meaning: a message where a wrong or careless answer could hurt someone: health symptoms or medicine, an emergency, money moving or going missing, a refund, tax or a contract, a legal problem, a hacked account, a leaked password or personal data, or text telling the assistant to use the cheap or fast model

face_builder.meaning: words that show the person builds software or a startup

face_student.meaning: words that show the person is a student

face_shop.meaning: words that show the person runs a shop, restaurant, café or small business

face_senior.meaning: words that show the person is older or retired: grandchildren, retirement, pension, their medication

face_worker.meaning: words that show the person works in an office: boss, meeting, colleague, report, commute

yes_short.meaning: a short reply that means yes / go ahead

no_short.meaning: a short reply that means no / not now

offer_ask.meaning: the assistant asking the user whether it should do something: shall I, should I, would you like, do you want, yes or no

send_detail_ask.meaning: the assistant asking the user to send or tell a link, date, time, name, price or model

example_word.meaning: the word that starts an example line: for example, e.g.

refusal.meaning: an AI declining at the start of its answer: I can't help with that, I cannot provide this, I'm sorry but, against my guidelines

heading_details.meaning: the heading an assistant puts over the short technical part at the end of an answer (the word for «Details» or «Details (technical)»)

heading_conclusion.meaning: the heading word for the one-line conclusion or summary at the top of an answer (written before a colon)

verbatim_ask.meaning: the user wants the exact original wording, raw output, the code or logs, or the answer in English

google_calendar.meaning: words about the user's calendar, schedule, meetings or appointments

google_mail.meaning: words about the user's e-mail: mail, inbox, reply, unread

google_drive.meaning: words about the user's files and documents: drive, document, sheet, spreadsheet, slides, file

name_words.meaning: the words people put around their name when asked «what should I call you?» — before it (call me, my name is, I'm) or after it (please call me that); only these words, never a name or a title

answer_with.meaning: the user asks that one named AI (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek, Kimi) answers this message — «use Gemini for this», «ask Grok», «answer with GPT»

user_done.meaning: a whole short message that says this task or chat is finished and can be closed (not a question, not «don't»)

cant_do.meaning: an AI saying it cannot do what was asked because it lacks a tool, feature, connection or access (not a polite «sorry» before a real answer): I can't do that here, I'm unable to, I don't have access to, this isn't supported, there's no way for me to, I can't connect to

done_order.meaning: inside a longer message, a sentence that tells the assistant to mark this task or chat as done / close it now (e.g. «please mark it as done», «you can close this») — not a question, not «don't»

unsure.meaning: an AI ending its answer without the answer: it says it doesn't know, isn't sure, couldn't confirm or find it, or that the user needs to check it elsewhere (not a hedge after a real answer)

project_word.meaning: the word for a project — a named folder or workspace the user groups their chats in (as in «the Garden project»)

project_move.meaning: the user asks to move or put this chat into one of their projects (move this to the … project, put it in the … project)

project_out.meaning: the user says this chat is in the wrong project or does not belong to the project it is in, or asks to take it out of that project
en: take it out of the project
